name: Motorcycle
description: Every motor vehicle with a seat or saddle for the operator designed to travel on no more than three wheels, including motor-driven cycles and motor scooters, whatever its weight or brake horsepower. An electric two-wheeler past the electric bicycle and motorized bicycle limits is one.

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle for the operator, and no more than three wheels on the ground (Ohio Revised Code §4511.01(C))
Takes in motor-driven cycles, motor scooters, autocycles and cab-enclosed motorcycles, regardless of weight or brake horsepower (Ohio Revised Code §4511.01(C))

An electric two-wheeler without pedals, or with a motor over 1 brake horsepower (750 W) or a top speed over 20 mph, can't be a motorized bicycle, so it is a motorcycle unless it qualifies as an electric bicycle
Riders need a two-wheel motorcycle license or endorsement, or a motor scooter one for a motor scooter
A temporary instruction permit is available from 15 years and 6 months after a knowledge test; permit holders ride in daylight only, without passengers, off interstates, and in a helmet and eyewear
Riders under 18 must hold the permit six months, complete driver education and a motorcycle safety course, and pass the skills test
Every rider and passenger must use safety glasses or other eye protection
Riders under 18, riders in their first, novice year, and their passengers must wear a DOT-approved helmet
Registered with the BMV, with a $14 license tax
One whose motor produces 5 brake horsepower (3,750 W) or less is barred from freeways
One designed mainly for use off streets and highways is an off-highway motorcycle instead
